children: Solid underlying net revenue growth of 4.0%* in Q3 and YTD 2026
Continued margin expansion with EBIT growth of 6.3% YTD 2026 (Q3 2026: 5.5%), despite increasing cost inflation and weather-related headwinds in parts of the Nordics in Q3
Strong free cash flow of DKK 1,164m YTD 2026, supporting the ongoing share buy-back
Plans toward 2029 are progressing as expected, with continued focus on own-brand growth and exploring new partnership opportunities
Full-year 2026 organic EBIT growth guidance narrowed to 6–8% from 6–10%
Lars Jensen, CEO of Royal Unibrew, comments:

"We delivered another quarter of solid commercial execution, with market share gains across most markets and continued improvement in profitability despite increasing inflationary pressure. The strength of our brands and commercial capabilities provides a solid foundation, and we are actively addressing higher input costs through pricing, cost, and efficiency measures. However, the inflationary environment remains uncertain and could put further pressure on consumer sentiment and discretionary spending. Against this backdrop, we have narrowed our full-year organic EBIT growth guidance to 6–8%.”
* Underlying net revenue growth was approximately 4% in Q3 and YTD 2026, excluding the exit from lower-margin activities

Commercial execution remained solid in Q3 2026, supporting market share gains in most markets and continued profitable growth. Key strategic categories performed well, with own brands remaining the main growth driver.
Volume growth reached 1.4% in Q3 2026 (YTD 2026: 1.6%), while net revenue increased by approximately 4% both in Q3 and YTD 2026, adjusted for the exit from lower-margin activities.

EBIT increased by 5.5% to DKK 820m in Q3 2026 (YTD 2026: +6.3% to DKK 1,845m), while the EBIT margin improved by 80 basis points, despite increasing inflationary pressure across several cost categories and continued long-term investments in our brands and commercial capabilities.
The organic EBIT growth guidance for full-year 2026 is narrowed to 6-8% from previously 6-10%. The updated guidance corresponds to EBIT of DKK 2,325–2,380m compared with DKK 2,202m in 2025.

The narrowing of the guidance range mainly reflects challenging market conditions in Finland, supply chain issues in BeNeLux and increasing cost inflation. In addition, EBIT is impacted by DKK 12m of accelerated amortization related to the PepsiCo partnership.
Net revenue for 2026 is expected to be slightly above 2025, reflecting continued growth in the beverage business, partly offset by the exit from the snack category and other lower-margin activities.
CAPEX is now expected in the level of 6% of net revenue, down from around 7% previously, reflecting the timing of some projects, with some investments now expected to fall into 2027.
The underlying assumptions remain unchanged and are described in further detail in the trading statement.
